messages:
andrew: Heads-up — saw a p95 latency blip in prod for microbatch workloads after the offload change yesterday. baseline was ~23ms, spike to ~46ms for some small requests.

maria: Ugh. Which offload change? the small-page threshold bump?

andrew: Yeah, we increased small-page offload threshold from 1KB -> 4KB to reduce VRAM pressure. It reduced overall GPU mem use but some tenants with lots of tiny KV lookups saw latency regressions.

yuki: Do you have a flame or perf sample?

andrew: Short snippet from the traces:
```
rpc_handler -> kvcache.lookup (hot) -> page-miss -> host-staging pin_wait ~12ms -> dma_submit ~6ms -> resume -> reply
```
Most interesting is multiple requests queued on the host-pinning path causing serial pin_wait.

maria: That fits. Offloading many small pages increases contention on the host staging pool (we only had 8 pinned staging slots per GPU).

sara: We also saw higher fragmentation in host pool — many tiny allocations cause scatter and extra bookkeeping.

andrew: Right. Two angles: reduce offload threshold (back to 2KB), or change staging pool semantics (per-tenant small-slot ring or ephemeral fast-pins).

yuki: Tradeoffs: lowering threshold gives more VRAM pressure. For some tenants VRAM will spike and fall back to slower evict which hurts bigger requests. Per-tenant small-slot is more complex but keeps global residency predictable.

maria: Another option: batch small pin ops. If we coalesce microbatch requests into a single host pin request per microbatch we can amortize the pin_wait. That requires microbatch-level KV aggregation (cheap).

andrew: Implemented a quick experiment: coalesced pins for microbatches (10k requests) -> p95 back to ~25ms, VRAM up by ~6%.

sara: Nice. Can you paste the config you used for the experiment?

andrew: Sure:
```json
{
  "offload_small_threshold": 2048,
  "staging_slots_per_gpu": 12,
  "microbatch_coalesce": true,
  "coalesce_window_ms": 5
}
```

yuki: coalesce_window_ms=5 is interesting. Low enough to keep latency but enough to gather a few pins. Did you see tail variance?

andrew: Tail improved, but some tenants with bursty single-shot RPCs saw 1-2ms added due to windowing. Overall p95 better.

maria: We should add a 'frag_score' metric to the host pool telemetry. That helps decide when compact-on-evict should run.

sara: Agree. Current telemetry only has free_slots and pinned_count. frag_score could be (1 - largest_contiguous / total_free).

yuki: Also consider "fastpath pins" backed by a small preallocated slab for tiny pages (<=512B). That avoids heavy allocator paths entirely.

andrew: Roadmap proposal:
- short-term: enable microbatch coalescing behind a feature flag for microbatch-heavy tenants. revert threshold to 2KB by default.
- medium: implement fastpath tiny-slab (512B) + frag_score telemetry + auto-compact trigger.
- long-term: per-tenant small-slot ring with QoS tokens.

maria: Sounds good. For medium term, compact-on-evict needs to be async and rate-limited. Compaction during busy periods causes stalls.

sara: We should also simulate mixed workloads (tiny KV + long generations) to ensure compaction doesn't regress large sequence latency. I can add a harness.

andrew: Please do. @infra-bot can you open an experiment ticket and assign to sara/maria/yuki? :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Created EXP-2024: "microbatch small-page offload: coalesce + tiny-slab experiment" assigned [sara, maria, yuki] with priority P1.

yuki: I'll take the tiny-slab design doc. Quick notes: need alignment with host mmap granularity and pin lifecycle, eviction racecases for transient slabs, and metrics for slab reuse hit-rate.

maria: I'll own frag_score + auto-compact heuristics. Will draft telemetry spec by EOD.

sara: I'll build the mixed-workload harness and run across staging clusters. Goal: reproduce the p95 spike reliably.

andrew: Thanks all. Happy to roll back threshold if experiments show regressions. For now I'm enabling coalesce behind feature flags on a few tenants. Will post results in 24h. :sparkles:
